# README.md

Source: https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml/blob/main/README.md

<p align="center">
  <img alt="nixtml logo" src="./logo.svg" width="1000px">
</p>

<p align="center">A static website generator written in <strong>nix</strong>. Inspired by hugo.</p>

## Getting started

```nix
{
  description = "My website generated using nixtml.";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    nixtml.url = "github:arnarg/nixtml";
  };

  outputs =
    {
      self,
      nixpkgs,
      flake-utils,
      nixtml,
    }:
    (flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (
      system:
      let
        pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in
      {
        packages.blog = nixtml.lib.mkWebsite {
          inherit pkgs;

          name = "my-blog";
          baseURL = "https://my-blog.com";

          # Arbitrary metdata to be used in
          # templates.
          metadata = {
            lang = "en";
            title = "My Blog";
            description = "This is my blog";
          };

          # Walk a directory of markdown files
          # and create a page for each of them.
          content.dir = ./content; 

          # Copy an entire directory and symlink
          # in the final website derivation.
          static.dir = ./static;

          # Collections are for paginating content
          # and generating RSS feeds.
          collections.blog = {
            path = "posts";

            # Posts in the collection should be
            # grouped by optional tags in posts'
            # frontmatter.
            taxonomies = [ "tags" ];
          };

          # Import any nixtml modules (good for
          # "themes").
          imports = [ ./theme.nix ];
        };

        # Quickly build and serve website with
        # `nix run .#serve`.
        apps.serve = {
          type = "app";
          program =
            (pkgs.writeShellScript "serve-blog" ''
              ${pkgs.python3}/bin/python -m http.server -d ${self.packages.${system}.blog} 8080
            '').outPath;
        };
      }
    ));
}
```

See all available nixtml module options [here](https://arnarg.github.io/nixtml/options/).

## Examples

- [My blog](https://github.com/arnarg/blog)

## Templates

Templates should be defined in modules under `website.layouts`. All templates should be a function to a string (or list of strings, that is automatically coerced to a string).

### Nix functional HTML

In nixtml's lib there are functions for most commonly used HTML tags which can be used like this:

```nix
{lib, ...}: let
  inherit (lib.tags)
    html
    head
    body
    div
    ;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in {
  website.layouts.base =
    { path, content, ... }@context:
    "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
    +
      html
        [ (attrs.lang metadata.lang) ]
        [
          (head [ ] [ (partials.head context) ])
          (body
            [
              (attrs.classes [
                "font-sans"
                "bg-white"
              ])
            ]
            [
              (div
                [
                  (attrs.classes [ "container" ])
                ]
                [ content ]
              )
            ]
          )
        ];
}
```

### Normal string templating

The above is equivalent to defining the markup using strings in nix:

```nix
{lib, ...}: {
  website.layouts.base =
    { path, content, ... }@context: ''
      <!DOCTYPE html>
      <html lang="${metadata.lang}">
        <head>
          ${partials.head context}
        </head>
        <body class="font-sant bg-white">
          <div class="container">
            ${content}
          </div>
        </body>
      </html>
    '';
}
```

### Standard templates

Each template in `website.layouts` has a specific purpose.

- `website.layouts.base`: Used for the skeleton of each HTML file for the website. It gets passed the result of other rendered templates.
- `website.layouts.hom`: Used for `./index.md`, if found in `website.content.dir`. It gets passed the metadata in the markdown frontmatter as well as the HTML content generated from markdown.
- `website.layouts.page`: Used for any other markdown file found in `website.content.dir`. It gets passed the metadata in the markdown frontmatter as well as the HTML content generated from markdown.
- `website.layouts.collection`: Used for pagination pages for collections.
- `website.layouts.taxonomy`: Used for pagination pages for taxonomies in collections.
- `website.layouts.partials`: An attribute set of templates (functions to string or list of strings) that can be used to reduce repitition in the other standard templates.

## Content

By setting `website.content.dir` nixtml will traverse that directory, transform any markdown file it finds and output an HTML file in the final website derivation with the same path. For example, `${content.dir}/about.md` becomes `about/index.html` in the final website derivation.

## Collections

Collections allow you to group, paginate and list related content such as blog posts or portfolio pieces.

Create a collection under `website.collections.<name>` and point it to a folder inside `website.content.dir`.

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";     # ./content/blog/posts/
  pagination.perPage = 5;  # Number of items each listing page shows
  rss.enable = true;       # Generate /blog/index.xml
};
```

nixtml automatically produces listing pages hosting `pagination.perPage` items per page (`blog/index.html`, `blog/page/2/index.html`, …) rendered with the `collection` layout template.

### Taxonomies

You may want to allow readers to explore entries by common key–words such as tags, categories or authors. Activate any number of taxonomies with the list key `taxonomies`:

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";
  taxonomies = [ "tags" "series" ];
};
```

In every markdown file inside that collection you can now list these terms in the YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
title: "My Emacs Setup"
date: 2024-07-15
tags:
  - emacs
  - productivity
series:
  - dotfiles
---
Post body…
```

nixtml will then create pages such as `/blog/tags/emacs/index.html`, `/blog/tags/emacs/page/2/index.html` and so on using the `taxonomy` layout template.

Inside collection or taxonomy templates you always receive the same context attribute set:

```nix
{
  # --- collection & taxonomy -------------
  pageNumber,     # Current page number
  totalPages,     # Total amount of pages
  items,          # List of posts in this page
  hasNext,        # A next page exists (bool)
  hasPrev,        # A previous page exists (bool)
  nextPageURL,    # URL to next page
  prevPageURL,    # URL to previous page
  # --- only taxonomy --------------------
  title,          # The tag or term being shown
}
```

## Examples

Look at the examples directory to see how to work with nixtml. They can be built with `nix build .#examples.simple` and `nix build .#examples.blog`.

# collections.md

Source: https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml/blob/main/docs/content/collections.md

title: Collections in nixtml
description: Learn how to organize content with collections

Collections allow you to group, paginate, and list related content such as blog posts, portfolio pieces, or any other content type that benefits from organization and pagination.

## What Collections Do

When you create a collection, nixtml automatically:

1. **Gathers content** from a specified directory
2. **Sorts items** by date (newest first)
3. **Creates pagination pages** for browsing items
4. **Generates RSS feeds** for syndication
5. **Creates taxonomy pages** for tags, categories, etc.

## Basic Collection Setup

Add a collection to your website configuration:

```nix
{
  website.collections.blog = {
    path = "posts";
    pagination.perPage = 5;
  };
}
```

### Understanding the Path

The `path` option determines both where content is read from and where pagination pages are created:

| `path` Value | Content Directory | Pagination URLs |
|--------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| `"posts"` | `./content/posts/` | `/index.html`, `/page/2/index.html` |
| `"blog/posts"` | `./content/blog/posts/` | `/blog/index.html`, `/blog/page/2/index.html` |
| `"writing/articles"` | `./content/writing/articles/` | `/writing/index.html`, `/writing/page/2/index.html` |

The pagination pages are created in the **parent directory** of the path.

## Directory Structure

A typical blog setup looks like this:

```
my-website/
├── flake.nix
├── layouts.nix
└── content/
    ├── index.md              # Homepage
    ├── about.md              # About page
    └── blog/
        └── posts/            # Collection content
            ├── first-post.md
            ├── second-post.md
            └── third-post.md
```

With the configuration:

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";
  pagination.perPage = 2;
};
```

This generates:

```
result/
├── index.html                # Homepage
├── about/index.html          # About page
├── blog/
│   ├── index.html            # Collection page 1 (2 posts)
│   ├── index.xml             # RSS feed
│   └── page/
│       └── 2/
│           └── index.html    # Collection page 2 (1 post)
└── blog/posts/
    ├── first-post/index.html
    ├── second-post/index.html
    └── third-post/index.html
```

## Writing Collection Content

Each markdown file in the collection needs proper frontmatter:

```markdown
---
title: My First Blog Post
date: 2026-01-15T10:00:00
tags:
  - nix
  - tutorial
---

This is the introduction paragraph that appears in listings.

<!--more-->

This content only appears on the full post page, not in summaries.
```

### Required Frontmatter

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `title` | Post title (displayed in listings) |
| `date` | Publication date in ISO 8601 format |

### The `<!--more-->` Tag

Use `<!--more-->` to mark where the summary ends:

```markdown
---
title: Understanding Nix Flakes
date: 2026-01-19
---

Nix flakes provide a standard way to write Nix expressions
with better reproducibility and composability.

<!--more-->

## What are Flakes?

Flakes are an experimental feature...
```

The `item.summary` in templates contains everything **before** the `<!--more-->` tag. If omitted, `summary` contains the entire content.

## Collection Configuration Options

```nix
website.collections.<name> = {
  # Required: Path to content within content.dir
  path = "posts";

  # Pagination settings
  pagination.perPage = 5;  # Default: 5

  # Taxonomy groupings
  taxonomies = [ "tags" "categories" ];  # Default: []

  # RSS feed settings
  rss.enable = true;   # Default: true
  rss.limit = 50;      # Default: 50
};
```

## Collection Item Properties

Each item in a collection has these properties available in templates:

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Post title from frontmatter |
| `date` | string | Formatted date (e.g., "Jan 15, 2026") |
| `dateEpoch` | number | Unix timestamp |
| `dateRFC822` | string | RFC 822 date for RSS feeds |
| `dateW3C` | string | W3C date format (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `url` | string | Relative URL (e.g., `/blog/posts/my-post`) |
| `permalink` | string | Full URL (e.g., `https://example.com/blog/posts/my-post`) |
| `content` | string | Full HTML content |
| `summary` | string | Content before `<!--more-->` |
| `metadata` | attrs | All other frontmatter fields |

## Collection Template

The `collection` layout renders pagination pages:

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (lib.tags) div h1 h2 ul li a p span article;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts.collection = {
    pageNumber,    # Current page (1, 2, 3...)
    totalPages,    # Total number of pages
    items,         # List of posts on this page
    hasNext,       # true if next page exists
    hasPrev,       # true if previous page exists
    nextPageURL,   # URL to next page (throws if !hasNext)
    prevPageURL,   # URL to previous page (throws if !hasPrev)
    ...
  }:
    [
      (h1 [] [ "Blog" ])

      # List of posts
      (div [ (attrs.class "posts") ]
        (map (item:
          article [ (attrs.class "post-preview") ] [
            (h2 [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ])
            (p [ (attrs.class "date") ] [ item.date ])
            (p [ (attrs.class "summary") ] [ item.summary ])
            (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ "Read more →" ])
          ]
        ) items)
      )

      # Pagination navigation
      (div [ (attrs.class "pagination") ] [
        (if hasPrev
          then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) (attrs.class "prev") ] [ "← Newer" ])
          else (span [ (attrs.class "prev disabled") ] [ "← Newer" ]))

        (span [ (attrs.class "page-info") ]
          [ "Page ${toString pageNumber} of ${toString totalPages}" ])

        (if hasNext
          then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) (attrs.class "next") ] [ "Older →" ])
          else (span [ (attrs.class "next disabled") ] [ "Older →" ]))
      ])
    ];
}
```

## Taxonomies

Taxonomies let readers browse content by category. See the [Taxonomies Guide](/nixtml/taxonomies) for full documentation.

### Quick Setup

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";
  taxonomies = [ "tags" "categories" ];
};
```

### In Content

```markdown
---
title: Getting Started with Nix
date: 2026-01-19
tags:
  - nix
  - beginner
categories:
  - tutorials
---
```

### Generated Pages

| Taxonomy Term | Page URL | RSS Feed |
|---------------|----------|----------|
| tags: nix | `/blog/tags/nix/index.html` | `/blog/tags/nix/index.xml` |
| tags: beginner | `/blog/tags/beginner/index.html` | `/blog/tags/beginner/index.xml` |
| categories: tutorials | `/blog/categories/tutorials/index.html` | `/blog/categories/tutorials/index.xml` |

### Taxonomy Template

```nix
website.layouts.taxonomy = {
  title,         # The taxonomy term (e.g., "nix")
  pageNumber,
  totalPages,
  items,
  hasNext,
  hasPrev,
  nextPageURL,
  prevPageURL,
  ...
}:
  [
    (h1 [] [ "Tagged: ${title}" ])
    (ul [] (map (item:
      li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ]
    ) items))
    # ... pagination controls
  ];
```

## RSS Feeds

RSS feeds are generated automatically when `rss.enable = true` (the default).

### Feed Locations

| Collection Config | RSS Feed URL |
|-------------------|--------------|
| `path = "posts"` | `/index.xml` |
| `path = "blog/posts"` | `/blog/index.xml` |

### Linking to RSS

Add a link in your base template:

```nix
(link [
  (attrs.rel "alternate")
  (attrs.type "application/rss+xml")
  (attrs.title "RSS Feed")
  (attrs.href "/blog/index.xml")
])
```

## Complete Example

Here's a full blog setup:

### `flake.nix`

```nix
{
  description = "My blog";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    nixtml.url = "github:arnarg/nixtml";
  };

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, flake-utils, nixtml }:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (system:
      let pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in {
        packages.default = nixtml.lib.mkWebsite {
          inherit pkgs;
          name = "my-blog";
          baseURL = "https://my-blog.com";

          metadata = {
            lang = "en";
            title = "My Blog";
            description = "Thoughts on Nix and programming";
          };

          content.dir = ./content;

          collections.blog = {
            path = "blog/posts";
            pagination.perPage = 5;
            taxonomies = [ "tags" ];
            rss.enable = true;
          };

          imports = [ ./layouts.nix ];
        };
      }
    );
}
```

### `layouts.nix`

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (config.website) metadata;
  inherit (lib.tags) html head body div h1 h2 ul li a p article nav span;
  inherit (lib.tags) title meta link;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts = {
    base = { path, content, ... }:
      "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
      + (html [ (attrs.lang metadata.lang) ] [
          (head [] [
            (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
            (title metadata.title)
            (link [
              (attrs.rel "alternate")
              (attrs.type "application/rss+xml")
              (attrs.href "/blog/index.xml")
            ])
          ])
          (body [] [
            (nav [] [
              (a [ (attrs.href "/") ] [ "Home" ])
              " | "
              (a [ (attrs.href "/blog") ] [ "Blog" ])
            ])
            (div [ (attrs.class "content") ] [ content ])
          ])
        ]);

    home = { content, ... }: content;

    page = { metadata, content, ... }: [
      (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])
      content
    ];

    collection = { pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, nextPageURL, prevPageURL, ... }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "Blog" ])
        (div [ (attrs.class "posts") ]
          (map (item:
            article [] [
              (h2 [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ])
              (p [] [ item.date ])
              (p [] [ item.summary ])
            ]
          ) items)
        )
        (div [ (attrs.class "pagination") ] [
          (if hasPrev then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) ] [ "← Newer" ]) else "")
          " Page ${toString pageNumber}/${toString totalPages} "
          (if hasNext then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) ] [ "Older →" ]) else "")
        ])
      ];

    taxonomy = { title, pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, nextPageURL, prevPageURL, ... }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "Tagged: ${title}" ])
        (ul []
          (map (item: li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ]) items)
        )
        (div [] [
          (if hasPrev then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) ] [ "← Prev" ]) else "")
          " Page ${toString pageNumber}/${toString totalPages} "
          (if hasNext then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) ] [ "Next →" ]) else "")
        ])
      ];
  };
}
```

### `content/blog/posts/hello-world.md`

```markdown
---
title: Hello World
date: 2026-01-19T10:00:00
tags:
  - announcements
---

Welcome to my new blog! I'll be writing about Nix and programming.

<!--more-->

## What to Expect

I plan to cover topics like:
- Nix flakes
- NixOS configuration
- Functional programming

Stay tuned!
```

## Multiple Collections

You can have multiple independent collections:

```nix
website.collections = {
  blog = {
    path = "blog/posts";
    pagination.perPage = 5;
    taxonomies = [ "tags" ];
  };

  projects = {
    path = "portfolio/projects";
    pagination.perPage = 10;
    rss.enable = false;  # No RSS for portfolio
  };

  notes = {
    path = "notes";
    pagination.perPage = 20;
    taxonomies = [ "topics" ];
  };
};
```

Each collection operates independently with its own pagination, taxonomies, and RSS feeds.

## Best Practices

1. **Use descriptive paths**: `blog/posts` is clearer than just `posts`
2. **Set appropriate pagination**: 5-10 items for blogs, more for portfolios
3. **Always include dates**: Required for proper sorting
4. **Use `<!--more-->` tags**: Keeps listing pages clean
5. **Consistent taxonomy terms**: Use lowercase, hyphenated terms
6. **Limit RSS feeds**: 20-50 items is usually sufficient

---

# Welcome to My Website

Source: https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml/blob/main/docs/content/index.md

title: Getting Started with nixtml
description: A step-by-step guide to creating your first website with nixtml

nixtml is a static website generator written in Nix, inspired by Hugo. This guide will walk you through creating your first website from scratch.

## Prerequisites

- **Nix** installed with flakes enabled
- Basic familiarity with Nix language
- A text editor

To enable flakes, add this to your `~/.config/nix/nix.conf`:

```
experimental-features = nix-command flakes
```

## Project Structure

By the end of this guide, your project will look like this:

```
my-website/
├── flake.nix          # Main configuration
├── content/
│   ├── index.md       # Homepage
│   └── about.md       # About page
└── static/            # Static assets (CSS, images, etc.)
    └── css/
        └── style.css
```

## Step 1: Create a New Project

```bash
mkdir my-website
cd my-website
```

## Step 2: Create the Flake Configuration

Create a `flake.nix` file:

```nix
{
  description = "My website generated using nixtml.";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    nixtml.url = "github:arnarg/nixtml";
  };

  outputs = {
    self,
    nixpkgs,
    flake-utils,
    nixtml,
  }:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (
      system:
      let
        pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in
      {
        packages.default = nixtml.lib.mkWebsite {
          inherit pkgs;

          name = "my-website";
          baseURL = "https://my-website.com";

          # Site-wide metadata available in templates
          metadata = {
            lang = "en";
            title = "My Website";
            description = "Welcome to my website";
          };

          # Directory containing markdown content
          content.dir = ./content;

          # Optional: Directory for static assets
          # static.dir = ./static;

          # Import layout configuration from separate file
          imports = [ ./layouts.nix ];
        };

        # Convenient local development server
        apps.serve = {
          type = "app";
          program =
            (pkgs.writeShellScript "serve" ''
              echo "Serving at http://localhost:8080"
              ${pkgs.python3}/bin/python -m http.server -d ${self.packages.${system}.default} 8080
            '').outPath;
        };
      }
    );
}
```

## Step 3: Create the Layouts

Create a `layouts.nix` file to define how your pages look:

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  # Access site metadata defined in flake.nix
  inherit (config.website) metadata;

  # Import HTML helper functions
  inherit (lib.tags)
    html
    head
    body
    div
    h1
    p
    a
    nav
    ul
    li
    meta
    ;
  inherit (lib.tags) title link;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts = {
    # Base template wraps all pages
    base = { path, content, ... }:
      "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
      + (html [ (attrs.lang metadata.lang) ] [
          (head [] [
            (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
            (meta [
              (attrs.name "viewport")
              (attrs.content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0")
            ])
            (meta [
              (attrs.name "description")
              (attrs.content metadata.description)
            ])
            (title metadata.title)
            # Uncomment when you add static/css/style.css
            # (link [
            #   (attrs.rel "stylesheet")
            #   (attrs.href "/css/style.css")
            # ])
          ])
          (body [] [
            (nav [] [
              (ul [] [
                (li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href "/") ] [ "Home" ]) ])
                (li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href "/about") ] [ "About" ]) ])
              ])
            ])
            (div [ (attrs.class "container") ] [ content ])
          ])
        ]);

    # Template for index.md (homepage)
    home = { content, ... }: content;

    # Template for all other pages
    page = { metadata, content, ... }: [
      (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])
      content
    ];

    # Required for collections (can be minimal for now)
    collection = { pageNumber, totalPages, items, ... }:
      (div [] [
        (ul [] (map (item: li [] [ item.title ]) items))
        "Page ${toString pageNumber} of ${toString totalPages}"
      ]);

    # Required for taxonomies (can be minimal for now)
    taxonomy = { title, pageNumber, totalPages, items, ... }:
      (div [] [
        (h1 [] [ title ])
        (ul [] (map (item: li [] [ item.title ]) items))
        "Page ${toString pageNumber} of ${toString totalPages}"
      ]);
  };
}
```

## Step 4: Create Content

Create the content directory and your first pages:

```bash
mkdir -p content
```

### Homepage (`content/index.md`)

```markdown
---
title: Home
date: 2026-01-19T00:00:00
---

# Welcome to My Website

This is the homepage of my nixtml-powered website.

Built with **Nix** for reproducible, declarative static site generation.
```

### About Page (`content/about.md`)

```markdown
---
title: About
date: 2026-01-19T00:00:00
---

This website was created using nixtml, a static site generator written in Nix.

## Why nixtml?

- Declarative configuration
- Reproducible builds
- Native Nix integration
- Markdown content with frontmatter
```

## Step 5: Build Your Website

```bash
nix build .#
```

This creates a `result` symlink pointing to your built website. Explore the output:

```bash
ls -la result/
```

You should see:

- `index.html` - Your homepage
- `about/index.html` - Your about page
- `sitemap.xml` - Auto-generated sitemap

## Step 6: Serve Locally

```bash
nix run .#serve
```

Open [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080) in your browser to see your website.

## Step 7: Add Styling (Optional)

Create a static directory with CSS:

```bash
mkdir -p static/css
```

Create `static/css/style.css`:

```css
* {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

body {
  font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: #333;
  max-width: 800px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 20px;
}

nav ul {
  list-style: none;
  padding: 0;
  display: flex;
  gap: 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;
  padding-bottom: 10px;
  margin-bottom: 20px;
}

nav a {
  text-decoration: none;
  color: #0066cc;
}

nav a:hover {
  text-decoration: underline;
}

h1 {
  color: #111;
}

.container {
  padding: 20px 0;
}
```

Then update your `flake.nix` to include static files:

```nix
# Uncomment this line in mkWebsite:
static.dir = ./static;
```

And uncomment the stylesheet link in `layouts.nix`.

Rebuild to see the changes:

```bash
nix run .#serve
```

## Understanding the Configuration

### `mkWebsite` Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `name` | Website name (used in derivation name) |
| `baseURL` | Full URL where site will be hosted |
| `metadata` | Arbitrary data available in all templates |
| `content.dir` | Directory containing markdown files |
| `static.dir` | Directory with static assets |
| `layouts` | Template functions for rendering pages |
| `imports` | Additional Nix modules to import |

### Template Context

Each template receives a context object:

- **base**: `{ path, content, ... }` - receives rendered content from child templates
- **home**: `{ content, metadata, ... }` - receives parsed markdown content
- **page**: `{ content, metadata, ... }` - receives parsed markdown content
- **collection**: `{ pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, ... }`
- **taxonomy**: `{ title, taxonomoy, pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, ... }`

### Frontmatter

Markdown files support YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
title: Page Title
date: 2026-01-19T00:00:00
customField: any value
---

Content here...
```

The frontmatter is available as `metadata` in your templates.

- **[Advanced Templating](/nixtml/templating)**: Master the Nix HTML library and partials
- **[Nixtml Module Options](/nixtml/options)**: View all available module options in nixtml

- **simple**: Basic website with pages
- **blog**: Full blog with collections, taxonomies, and RSS feeds

# Good

Source: https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml/blob/main/docs/content/taxonomies.md

title: Taxonomies in nixtml
description: Organize your content with tags, categories, and custom taxonomies

Taxonomies provide a way to classify and organize your content, making it easier for readers to find related posts. nixtml supports custom taxonomies like tags, categories, authors, series, and any other grouping you need.

## What Are Taxonomies?

Taxonomies are classification systems for your content. Each taxonomy has **terms** (values), and content can have multiple terms per taxonomy.

**Common taxonomy examples:**

| Taxonomy | Terms | Use Case |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `tags` | nix, tutorial, beginner | Specific keywords |
| `categories` | programming, guides | Broad topics |
| `authors` | john-doe, jane-smith | Content creators |
| `series` | nix-basics, advanced-flakes | Multi-part content |
| `difficulty` | beginner, intermediate | Skill levels |

## Quick Start

### 1. Enable Taxonomies

Add taxonomies to your collection:

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";
  taxonomies = [ "tags" ];
};
```

### 2. Add Terms to Content

In your markdown frontmatter:

```markdown
---
title: Getting Started with Nix
date: 2026-01-19
tags:
  - nix
  - beginner
  - tutorial
---

Your content here...
```

### 3. Define the Taxonomy Template

```nix
website.layouts.taxonomy = { title, items, ... }:
  [
    (h1 [] [ "Posts tagged: ${title}" ])
    (ul [] (map (item: li [] [ item.title ]) items))
  ];
```

That's it! nixtml automatically generates pages for each tag.

## Generated URLs

Taxonomy pages are created based on your collection's path:

### Example: `path = "blog/posts"`

| Content | Generated URL |
|---------|---------------|
| Tag page: nix | `/blog/tags/nix/index.html` |
| Tag page 2: nix | `/blog/tags/nix/page/2/index.html` |
| RSS feed: nix | `/blog/tags/nix/index.xml` |
| Category page | `/blog/categories/tutorials/index.html` |

### Example: `path = "posts"`

| Content | Generated URL |
|---------|---------------|
| Tag page: nix | `/tags/nix/index.html` |
| RSS feed: nix | `/tags/nix/index.xml` |

The pattern is: `/{collection-prefix}/{taxonomy}/{term}/`

## Taxonomy Template

The `taxonomy` layout receives these context variables:

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `title` | string | The taxonomy term (e.g., "nix") |
| `pageNumber` | int | Current page number (1-indexed) |
| `totalPages` | int | Total number of pages |
| `items` | list | Posts on this page |
| `hasNext` | bool | Whether next page exists |
| `hasPrev` | bool | Whether previous page exists |
| `nextPageURL` | string | URL to next page |
| `prevPageURL` | string | URL to previous page |

### Complete Template Example

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (lib.tags) div h1 h2 ul li a p span article;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts.taxonomy = {
    title,
    pageNumber,
    totalPages,
    items,
    hasNext,
    hasPrev,
    nextPageURL,
    prevPageURL,
    ...
  }:
    [
      # Header with term name
      (h1 [] [ "Posts tagged: #${title}" ])

      # Post count
      (p [ (attrs.class "taxonomy-meta") ]
        [ "${toString (builtins.length items)} posts" ])

      # List of posts
      (div [ (attrs.class "post-list") ]
        (map (item:
          article [ (attrs.class "post-preview") ] [
            (h2 [] [
              (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ])
            ])
            (div [ (attrs.class "post-meta") ] [
              (span [ (attrs.class "date") ] [ item.date ])
            ])
            (p [ (attrs.class "summary") ] [ item.summary ])
          ]
        ) items)
      )

      # Pagination
      (div [ (attrs.class "pagination") ] [
        (if hasPrev
          then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) (attrs.class "prev") ] [ "← Newer Posts" ])
          else (span [ (attrs.class "prev disabled") ] [ "← Newer Posts" ]))

        (span [ (attrs.class "page-info") ]
          [ "Page ${toString pageNumber} of ${toString totalPages}" ])

        (if hasNext
          then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) (attrs.class "next") ] [ "Older Posts →" ])
          else (span [ (attrs.class "next disabled") ] [ "Older Posts →" ]))
      ])
    ];
}
```

## Displaying Tags on Posts

To show tags on individual posts, access them via `metadata`:

### In the Page Template

```nix
website.layouts.page = { metadata, content, ... }:
  let
    # Get tags, defaulting to empty list
    tags = metadata.tags or [];
  in
  [
    (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])

    # Show tags if present
    (if tags != [] then
      (div [ (attrs.class "tags") ]
        (map (tag:
          a [
            (attrs.href "/blog/tags/${tag}")
            (attrs.class "tag")
          ] [ "#${tag}" ]
        ) tags)
      )
    else "")

    # Post content
    (div [ (attrs.class "content") ] [ content ])
  ];
```

### In Collection Listings

```nix
website.layouts.collection = { items, ... }:
  (div []
    (map (item:
      article [] [
        (h2 [] [ item.title ])
        (p [] [ item.date ])

        # Tags from item.metadata
        (if (item.metadata.tags or []) != [] then
          (div [ (attrs.class "tags") ]
            (map (tag:
              a [ (attrs.href "/blog/tags/${tag}") ] [ "#${tag}" ]
            ) item.metadata.tags)
          )
        else "")
      ]
    ) items)
  );
```

## Multiple Taxonomy Types

You can have any number of taxonomies:

```nix
website.collections.blog = {
  path = "blog/posts";
  taxonomies = [
    "tags"
    "categories"
    "authors"
    "series"
  ];
};
```

### Content with Multiple Taxonomies

```markdown
---
title: Building a Blog with Nix
date: 2026-01-19
tags:
  - nix
  - web
categories:
  - tutorials
authors:
  - john-doe
series:
  - nix-web-dev
---
```

This creates pages at:

- `/blog/tags/nix/`
- `/blog/tags/web/`
- `/blog/categories/tutorials/`
- `/blog/authors/john-doe/`
- `/blog/series/nix-web-dev/`

## RSS Feeds for Taxonomies

Each taxonomy term automatically gets an RSS feed:

| Term | RSS Feed URL |
|------|--------------|
| tags: nix | `/blog/tags/nix/index.xml` |
| categories: tutorials | `/blog/categories/tutorials/index.xml` |

Link to taxonomy RSS feeds in your templates:

```nix
website.layouts.taxonomy = { title, ... }:
  [
    (h1 [] [ "Posts tagged: ${title}" ])

    # RSS feed link
    (a [
      (attrs.href "/blog/tags/${title}/index.xml")
      (attrs.class "rss-link")
    ] [ "RSS Feed for #${title}" ])

    # ... rest of template
  ];
```

## Taxonomy Naming Conventions

### Recommended Practices

| Do | Don't |
|----|-------|
| `nix-flakes` | `Nix Flakes` |
| `getting-started` | `Getting Started` |
| `javascript` | `JavaScript` |
| `john-doe` | `John Doe` |

- **Use lowercase**: Avoids case-sensitivity issues
- **Use hyphens**: Creates clean URLs
- **Be consistent**: Same term should always be spelled the same

### URL-Safe Terms

Terms become part of URLs, so keep them URL-friendly:

```markdown
# Good
tags:
  - nix-flakes
  - getting-started

# Avoid
tags:
  - "Nix Flakes"      # Spaces in URLs
  - "C++"             # Special characters
```

## Complete Example

### Directory Structure

```
my-blog/
├── flake.nix
├── layouts.nix
└── content/
    └── blog/
        └── posts/
            ├── nix-intro.md
            ├── flakes-deep-dive.md
            └── nixos-config.md
```

### `content/blog/posts/nix-intro.md`

```markdown
---
title: Introduction to Nix
date: 2026-01-15
tags:
  - nix
  - beginner
categories:
  - tutorials
---

A beginner-friendly introduction to Nix.

<!--more-->

## What is Nix?

Nix is a powerful package manager...
```

### `flake.nix`

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    nixtml.url = "github:arnarg/nixtml";
  };

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, flake-utils, nixtml }:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (system:
      let pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in {
        packages.default = nixtml.lib.mkWebsite {
          inherit pkgs;
          name = "my-blog";
          baseURL = "https://my-blog.com";

          metadata = {
            lang = "en";
            title = "My Blog";
          };

          content.dir = ./content;

          collections.blog = {
            path = "blog/posts";
            pagination.perPage = 5;
            taxonomies = [ "tags" "categories" ];
          };

          imports = [ ./layouts.nix ];
        };
      }
    );
}
```

### `layouts.nix`

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (config.website) metadata;
  inherit (lib.tags) html head body div h1 h2 ul li a p span article nav;
  inherit (lib.tags) title meta link;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts = {
    base = { path, content, ... }:
      "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
      + (html [ (attrs.lang metadata.lang) ] [
          (head [] [
            (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
            (title metadata.title)
          ])
          (body [] [ content ])
        ]);

    home = { content, ... }: content;

    page = { metadata, content, ... }:
      let tags = metadata.tags or [];
      in [
        (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])
        (if tags != [] then
          (div [ (attrs.class "tags") ]
            (map (tag: a [ (attrs.href "/blog/tags/${tag}") ] [ "#${tag} " ]) tags)
          )
        else "")
        content
      ];

    collection = { pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, nextPageURL, prevPageURL, ... }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "Blog" ])
        (div [] (map (item:
          article [] [
            (h2 [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ])
            (p [] [ item.date ])
          ]
        ) items))
        (div [] [
          (if hasPrev then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) ] [ "← Newer" ]) else "")
          " Page ${toString pageNumber}/${toString totalPages} "
          (if hasNext then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) ] [ "Older →" ]) else "")
        ])
      ];

    taxonomy = { title, pageNumber, totalPages, items, hasNext, hasPrev, nextPageURL, prevPageURL, ... }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "#${title}" ])
        (p [] [ "${toString (builtins.length items)} posts" ])
        (ul [] (map (item:
          li [] [
            (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ])
            " - ${item.date}"
          ]
        ) items))
        (div [] [
          (if hasPrev then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) ] [ "← Newer" ]) else "")
          " Page ${toString pageNumber}/${toString totalPages} "
          (if hasNext then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) ] [ "Older →" ]) else "")
        ])
      ];
  };
}
```

## Best Practices

### Content Organization

- **Tags** (5-15 per post): Specific, descriptive keywords
- **Categories** (1-3 per post): Broad content types
- **Series**: Multi-part tutorials or related posts
- **Authors**: Multi-author blogs

### Performance

- Keep taxonomy count reasonable (3-5 types max)
- Use pagination for terms with many posts
- RSS feed limits help with large sites

### User Experience

- Display tags prominently on posts
- Provide navigation between related tags
- Consider a tag cloud or popular tags section
- Link to RSS feeds for individual tags

### SEO

- Use descriptive, keyword-rich terms
- Keep URLs clean with lowercase hyphenated terms
- Ensure taxonomy pages have good meta descriptions

---

# Examples

Source: https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml/blob/main/docs/content/templating.md

title: Advanced Templating
description: Learn about nixtml's powerful templating system

nixtml provides a flexible templating system using pure Nix functions. You can use either string interpolation for simple templates or the functional HTML library for type-safe markup.

## Template Types

nixtml requires these templates:

| Template | Purpose | Context |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `base` | Wraps all pages (HTML skeleton) | `path`, `content`, `title` |
| `home` | Renders `index.md` | `metadata`, `content` |
| `page` | Renders other markdown files | `metadata`, `content` |
| `collection` | Renders collection pagination | `items`, `pageNumber`, etc. |
| `taxonomy` | Renders taxonomy pages | `title`, `items`, etc. |
| `partials` | Reusable components | User-defined |

## Two Approaches to Templating

### 1. String Templates (Simple)

Use Nix string interpolation:

```nix
website.layouts.base = { path, content, ... }: ''
  <!DOCTYPE html>
  <html lang="en">
    <head>
      <meta charset="UTF-8">
      <title>My Website</title>
    </head>
    <body>
      ${content}
    </body>
  </html>
'';
```

### 2. Functional HTML (Fun?)

Use nixtml's tag functions:

```nix
{ lib, ... }:
let
  inherit (lib.tags) html head body meta title div;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
in
{
  website.layouts.base = { path, content, ... }:
    "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
    + (html [ (attrs.lang "en") ] [
        (head [] [
          (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
          (title "My Website")
        ])
        (body [] [ content ])
      ]);
}
```

## The Functional HTML Library

### How Tags Work

Tag functions have this signature:

```nix
tagName [ attributes ] [ children ]
```

- **First argument**: List of attributes (can be empty `[]`)
- **Second argument**: List of children (strings or nested tags)

```nix
# Examples
(div [] [ "Hello" ])                    # <div>Hello</div>
(div [ (attrs.class "box") ] [ "Hi" ])  # <div class="box">Hi</div>
(a [ (attrs.href "/") ] [ "Home" ])     # <a href="/">Home</a>
```

### Available Tags

#### Regular Tags (with closing tag)

```nix
inherit (lib.tags)
  # Document structure
  html head body

  # Sections
  header footer main nav section article aside

  # Headings
  h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6

  # Text content
  p div span pre blockquote

  # Lists
  ul ol li dl dt dd

  # Inline text
  a em strong code b i u s small

  # Tables
  table thead tbody tfoot tr th td

  # Forms
  form fieldset legend label button select option textarea

  # Media
  figure figcaption picture audio video

  # Other
  script style noscript template
  ;
```

#### Void Tags (self-closing)

```nix
inherit (lib.tags)
  meta link img input br hr
  area base col embed source track wbr
  ;
```

Void tags only take attributes:

```nix
(meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])           # <meta charset="UTF-8">
(link [ (attrs.rel "stylesheet") (attrs.href "/style.css") ])
(img [ (attrs.src "/logo.png") (attrs.alt "Logo") ])
(br [])                                       # <br>
```

#### Special: title Tag

The `title` tag has a convenience form:

```nix
(title "My Page Title")   # <title>My Page Title</title>
```

### Attributes Library

The `attrs` module provides attribute helpers:

```nix
inherit (lib) attrs;

# Common attributes
(attrs.id "main")           # id="main"
(attrs.class "container")   # class="container"
(attrs.href "/about")       # href="/about"
(attrs.src "/image.png")    # src="/image.png"
(attrs.alt "Description")   # alt="Description"
(attrs.type "text")         # type="text"
(attrs.name "email")        # name="email"
(attrs.content "value")     # content="value"
(attrs.rel "stylesheet")    # rel="stylesheet"
(attrs.lang "en")           # lang="en"
(attrs.charset "UTF-8")     # charset="UTF-8"
(attrs.target "_blank")     # target="_blank"
(attrs.title "Hover text")  # title="Hover text"

# Width/height (accepts int or string)
(attrs.width 100)           # width="100"
(attrs.height "auto")       # height="auto"

# Multiple classes
(attrs.classes [ "flex" "items-center" "gap-4" ])  # class="flex items-center gap-4"

# Data attributes
(attrs.data "theme" "dark")   # data-theme="dark"
(attrs.data "count" "5")      # data-count="5"

# ARIA attributes
(attrs.aria "label" "Menu")   # aria-label="Menu"
(attrs.aria "hidden" "true")  # aria-hidden="true"

# Meta attributes
(attrs.property "og:title")   # property="og:title"
(attrs.httpEquiv "refresh")   # http-equiv="refresh"
(attrs.itemprop "name")       # itemprop="name"
```

### Creating Custom Attributes

Use `lib.mkAttr` for attributes not in the library:

```nix
let
  customAttr = lib.mkAttr "data-custom" "value";
in
(div [ customAttr ] [ "Content" ])
# <div data-custom="value">Content</div>
```

## Template Context Reference

### Base Template

```nix
website.layouts.base = {
  path,      # List of path segments: [ "about" "index.html" ]
  content,   # Rendered HTML from child template
  title,     # Page title (null for collection/taxonomy pages)
  ...        # Additional context passed from child templates
}: ...;
```

### Home Template

```nix
website.layouts.home = {
  path,       # Always [ "index.html" ]
  metadata,   # Frontmatter from index.md
  content,    # HTML from markdown
  title,      # metadata.title
  ...
}: ...;
```

### Page Template

```nix
website.layouts.page = {
  path,       # [ "about" "index.html" ]
  metadata,   # Frontmatter from markdown file
  content,    # HTML from markdown
  title,      # metadata.title
  ...
}: ...;
```

### Collection Template

```nix
website.layouts.collection = {
  path,         # [ "blog" "index.html" ] or [ "blog" "page" "2" "index.html" ]
  pageNumber,   # Current page (1, 2, 3...)
  totalPages,   # Total number of pages
  items,        # List of posts on this page
  hasNext,      # true if next page exists
  hasPrev,      # true if previous page exists
  nextPageURL,  # URL string (throws if !hasNext)
  prevPageURL,  # URL string (throws if !hasPrev)
  title,        # Always null for collections
  ...
}: ...;
```

### Taxonomy Template

```nix
website.layouts.taxonomy = {
  path,         # [ "blog" "tags" "nix" "index.html" ]
  title,        # The taxonomy term ("nix")
  pageNumber,   # Current page number
  totalPages,   # Total pages for this term
  items,        # Posts with this term
  hasNext,      # true if next page exists
  hasPrev,      # true if previous page exists
  nextPageURL,  # URL to next page
  prevPageURL,  # URL to previous page
  ...
}: ...;
```

## Partials

Partials are reusable template functions:

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (lib.tags) header nav ul li a footer p div;
  inherit (lib) attrs;
  inherit (config.website) metadata;
  inherit (config.website.layouts) partials;
in
{
  website.layouts = {
    partials = {
      # Navigation partial
      navigation = { currentPath }:
        let
          isActive = href: if href == currentPath then "active" else "";
          navItem = href: label:
            li [ (attrs.class (isActive href)) ] [
              (a [ (attrs.href href) ] [ label ])
            ];
        in
        nav [ (attrs.class "main-nav") ] [
          (ul [] [
            (navItem "/" "Home")
            (navItem "/blog" "Blog")
            (navItem "/about" "About")
          ])
        ];

      # Footer partial
      siteFooter = { }:
        footer [ (attrs.class "site-footer") ] [
          (p [] [ "© 2026 ${metadata.title}" ])
          (p [] [ "Built with nixtml" ])
        ];

      # Meta tags partial
      metaTags = { title, description ? metadata.description }:
        [
          (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
          (meta [ (attrs.name "viewport") (attrs.content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1") ])
          (meta [ (attrs.name "description") (attrs.content description) ])
          (lib.tags.title title)
        ];
    };

    # Use partials in base template
    base = { path, content, title, ... }:
      let
        pageTitle = if title != null then "${title} - ${metadata.title}" else metadata.title;
        currentPath = "/" + lib.concatStringsSep "/" (lib.init path);
      in
      "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
      + (html [ (attrs.lang "en") ] [
          (head [] (partials.metaTags { title = pageTitle; }))
          (body [] [
            (partials.navigation { inherit currentPath; })
            (div [ (attrs.class "content") ] [ content ])
            (partials.siteFooter {})
          ])
        ]);
  };
}
```

## Conditional Rendering

### Simple Conditionals

```nix
website.layouts.page = { metadata, content, ... }:
  [
    # Show title if it exists
    (if metadata ? title then (h1 [] [ metadata.title ]) else "")

    content

    # Show date if present
    (if metadata ? date then (p [ (attrs.class "date") ] [ metadata.date ]) else "")
  ];
```

### With Default Values

```nix
website.layouts.page = { metadata, content, ... }:
  let
    # Provide defaults
    pageTitle = metadata.title or "Untitled";
    showToc = metadata.toc or false;
    tags = metadata.tags or [];
  in
  [
    (h1 [] [ pageTitle ])

    (if showToc then (div [ (attrs.class "toc") ] [ "Table of Contents..." ]) else "")

    content

    (if tags != [] then
      (div [ (attrs.class "tags") ]
        (map (tag: span [ (attrs.class "tag") ] [ tag ]) tags))
    else "")
  ];
```

## Working with Lists

### Mapping Over Items

```nix
# Simple list
(ul []
  (map (item: li [] [ item.title ]) items))

# With links
(ul []
  (map (item:
    li [] [
      (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ])
    ]
  ) items))

# Complex items
(div [ (attrs.class "posts") ]
  (map (item:
    article [ (attrs.class "post") ] [
      (h2 [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ])
      (p [ (attrs.class "date") ] [ item.date ])
      (p [ (attrs.class "summary") ] [ item.summary ])
    ]
  ) items))
```

## String Returns vs List Returns

Templates can return either strings or lists:

```nix
# String return
website.layouts.page = { content, ... }:
  "<article>${content}</article>";

# List return (automatically joined with newlines)
website.layouts.page = { metadata, content, ... }:
  [
    (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])
    content
  ];

# Mixed (nested lists are flattened)
website.layouts.base = { content, ... }:
  [
    "<!DOCTYPE html>"
    (html [] [
      (head [] [ ... ])
      (body [] [ content ])
    ])
  ];
```

## Escaping HTML

Use `lib.escapeHTML` to escape user content:

```nix
let
  inherit (lib) escapeHTML;

  # Escape special characters
  userInput = escapeHTML "<script>alert('xss')</script>";
  # Result: "&lt;script&gt;alert('xss')&lt;/script&gt;"
in
(p [] [ userInput ])
```

## Accessing Site Configuration

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  # Access website configuration
  inherit (config.website) metadata baseURL baseURI;

  # metadata contains your custom fields
  siteTitle = metadata.title;
  siteLang = metadata.lang;

  # URLs
  fullUrl = baseURL;       # "https://example.com"
  basePath = baseURI;      # "/" or "/blog/" if baseURL has path
in
{
  website.layouts.base = { path, content, ... }:
    ...;
}
```

## Complete Example

```nix
{ lib, config, ... }:
let
  inherit (config.website) metadata baseURL;
  inherit (config.website.layouts) partials;

  inherit (lib.tags)
    html head body
    header main footer nav
    div section article
    h1 h2 h3
    p span a
    ul ol li
    meta link
    time img
    ;
  inherit (lib.tags) title;
  inherit (lib) attrs escapeHTML;
in
{
  website.layouts = {
    # Reusable partials
    partials = {
      head = { pageTitle, description ? metadata.description }:
        [
          (meta [ (attrs.charset "UTF-8") ])
          (meta [ (attrs.name "viewport") (attrs.content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1") ])
          (meta [ (attrs.name "description") (attrs.content description) ])
          (meta [ (attrs.property "og:title") (attrs.content pageTitle) ])
          (meta [ (attrs.property "og:type") (attrs.content "website") ])
          (title pageTitle)
          (link [ (attrs.rel "stylesheet") (attrs.href "/css/style.css") ])
          (link [ (attrs.rel "alternate") (attrs.type "application/rss+xml") (attrs.href "/blog/index.xml") ])
        ];

      header = { }:
        header [ (attrs.class "site-header") ] [
          (div [ (attrs.class "container") ] [
            (a [ (attrs.href "/") (attrs.class "logo") ] [ metadata.title ])
            (nav [ (attrs.class "main-nav") ] [
              (ul [] [
                (li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href "/") ] [ "Home" ]) ])
                (li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href "/blog") ] [ "Blog" ]) ])
                (li [] [ (a [ (attrs.href "/about") ] [ "About" ]) ])
              ])
            ])
          ])
        ];

      footer = { }:
        footer [ (attrs.class "site-footer") ] [
          (div [ (attrs.class "container") ] [
            (p [] [ "© 2026 ${metadata.title}. All rights reserved." ])
            (p [] [
              "Built with "
              (a [ (attrs.href "https://github.com/arnarg/nixtml") ] [ "nixtml" ])
            ])
          ])
        ];

      postMeta = { item }:
        div [ (attrs.class "post-meta") ] [
          (time [ (attrs.data "datetime" item.dateW3C) ] [ item.date ])
          (if (item.metadata.tags or []) != [] then
            (span [ (attrs.class "tags") ]
              (map (tag:
                a [ (attrs.href "/blog/tags/${tag}") (attrs.class "tag") ] [ "#${tag}" ]
              ) item.metadata.tags))
          else "")
        ];
    };

    # Base template
    base = { path, content, title, ... }:
      let
        pageTitle = if title != null
          then "${title} - ${metadata.title}"
          else metadata.title;
      in
      "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
      + (html [ (attrs.lang metadata.lang) ] [
          (head [] (partials.head { inherit pageTitle; }))
          (body [ (attrs.class "page") ] [
            (partials.header {})
            (main [ (attrs.class "main-content") ] [
              (div [ (attrs.class "container") ] [ content ])
            ])
            (partials.footer {})
          ])
        ]);

    # Homepage
    home = { content, ... }:
      section [ (attrs.class "homepage") ] [
        content
      ];

    # Regular pages
    page = { metadata, content, ... }:
      article [ (attrs.class "page-content") ] [
        (header [] [
          (h1 [] [ metadata.title ])
          (if metadata ? date then
            (time [] [ metadata.date ])
          else "")
        ])
        (div [ (attrs.class "content") ] [ content ])
      ];

    # Collection listing
    collection = {
      pageNumber,
      totalPages,
      items,
      hasNext,
      hasPrev,
      nextPageURL,
      prevPageURL,
      ...
    }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "Blog" ])

        (div [ (attrs.class "posts") ]
          (map (item:
            article [ (attrs.class "post-preview") ] [
              (h2 [] [ (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ]) ])
              (partials.postMeta { inherit item; })
              (p [ (attrs.class "summary") ] [ item.summary ])
              (a [ (attrs.href item.url) (attrs.class "read-more") ] [ "Read more →" ])
            ]
          ) items))

        (nav [ (attrs.class "pagination") ] [
          (if hasPrev
            then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) (attrs.class "prev") ] [ "← Newer Posts" ])
            else (span [ (attrs.class "prev disabled") ] [ "← Newer Posts" ]))
          (span [ (attrs.class "page-info") ] [ "Page ${toString pageNumber} of ${toString totalPages}" ])
          (if hasNext
            then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) (attrs.class "next") ] [ "Older Posts →" ])
            else (span [ (attrs.class "next disabled") ] [ "Older Posts →" ]))
        ])
      ];

    # Taxonomy pages
    taxonomy = {
      title,
      pageNumber,
      totalPages,
      items,
      hasNext,
      hasPrev,
      nextPageURL,
      prevPageURL,
      ...
    }:
      [
        (h1 [] [ "Posts tagged #${title}" ])
        (p [ (attrs.class "taxonomy-meta") ] [ "${toString (builtins.length items)} posts" ])

        (ul [ (attrs.class "post-list") ]
          (map (item:
            li [] [
              (a [ (attrs.href item.url) ] [ item.title ])
              (span [ (attrs.class "date") ] [ " — ${item.date}" ])
            ]
          ) items))

        (nav [ (attrs.class "pagination") ] [
          (if hasPrev then (a [ (attrs.href prevPageURL) ] [ "← Newer" ]) else "")
          (span [] [ " Page ${toString pageNumber}/${toString totalPages} " ])
          (if hasNext then (a [ (attrs.href nextPageURL) ] [ "Older →" ]) else "")
        ])
      ];
  };
}
```

## Tips and Best Practices

1. **Start simple**: Begin with string templates, then refactor to functional HTML
2. **Use partials**: Extract repeated markup into partials
3. **Prefer functional HTML**: It catches typos and provides structure
4. **Escape user input**: Use `escapeHTML` for any dynamic content
5. **Keep templates focused**: Complex logic should live outside templates
6. **Test incrementally**: Build and check after each change

---
